title: U.S. House · Virginia's 8th District
area: Northern Virginia, including Arlington, Alexandria, Falls Church and parts of Fairfax County.

context.text: Incumbent Don Beyer won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 67.6% of the vote over Mo Seifeldein (17.6%), Adam Dunigan (9.0%), Michael Duffin (3.2%) and Lorena Bruner (2.6%). Tony Sabio advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after it was canceled. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate the race Solid/Safe Democratic as of September 22, 2026.

candidates.name: Donald Sternoff Beyer Jr.
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 67.6% of the vote.

priorities.text: Opposing the Trump administration's tariffs and tax cuts for high earners.
priorities.quote: I've helped focus counterattacks on Trump's tariffs, tax cuts for the rich, and broader economic record. I will not shy away from challenging this lawless president, or for standing up for federal workers and contractors, immigrants, LGBTQ+ people, and all those who have unjustly come under threat.

priorities.text: Building a more equitable economy, including universal paid leave, gun-violence prevention and climate action.
priorities.quote: creating a more equitable economy, ensuring everyone is treated fairly, supporting workers and guaranteeing them universal paid leave, fighting gun violence, and winning the fight against climate change.

priorities.text: Expanding the Affordable Housing Tax Credit and extending health-care tax credits to lower costs.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I have championed expansion of the Affordable Housing Tax Credit to spur the construction of new homes and bring down housing prices. I've helped pass legislation that would extend health care tax credits that make health coverage more affordable.

positions.summary: Says eliminating tariffs is one of the most effective steps to make life more affordable for Americans.
positions.quote: Eliminating Trump's tariffs is one of the most effective steps we can take to make life affordable for the American people.

positions.summary: Says he helped pass legislation extending health-care tax credits that make health coverage more affordable.
Lists fighting gun violence and climate change among his priorities, and opposed legislation he said would drive up electricity prices by killing clean-energy investment.
His official issues page says he supports a background check on every gun sale, restrictions on weapons designed for the battlefield, and red flag (risk protection order) laws.
positions.quote: I strongly believe we should enact laws requiring a background check on every gun sale to help keep guns out of the hands of criminals.

positions.summary: His official healthcare page criticizes the Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade and says the protections it provided should be restored and codified.
positions.quote: I was outraged by the Supreme Court’s decision to eliminate the protections women enjoyed for half a century under Roe v. Wade.

positions.summary: His official economy page lists asking the wealthy and large corporations to pay their fair share in taxes among his near-term priorities.
positions.quote: asking the wealthy and large corporations to pay their fair share in taxes to finance further investments in American workers and infrastructure

positions.summary: His official economy page says Congress must raise the minimum wage.
positions.quote: We must raise the minimum wage, end government shutdowns and brinksmanship over spending, and promote tax policies that empower workers and grow the middle class.

positions.summary: His official education page says he opposes vouchers and "school choice" initiatives that would undermine public schools.
positions.quote: I oppose any initiative (like vouchers or “school choice”) that would undermine our public schools or re-segregate our society.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and the Joint Economic Committee.

candidates.name: Tony Sabio
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after the primary was canceled.

priorities.text: Introducing legislation on day one covering national security, small business tax relief, workforce apprenticeships and critical-infrastructure protection.
priorities.quote: On day one, I will introduce the Nuclear-Ready Grid Zone Act, Nuclear Workforce Act, Small Business Tax Relief & Growth Act, Workforce Apprenticeship Act, and Small Business Continuity Protection Act.

priorities.text: Staying closely connected to constituents on cost of living, jobs, safety and economic stability.
Reducing political division in Congress and focusing on practical, results-oriented governing.

positions.summary: His campaign health plan proposes market-based coverage with guaranteed access for preexisting conditions and a time-limited, state-administered safety net, and contrasts it with Medicare for All and the ACA's subsidies.
positions.quote: This plan delivers universal access without a government takeover and lowers costs without permanent subsidies

statements.quote: Secure the border while restoring lawful and orderly immigration processes.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Safe Communities & Secure America Act page

statements.quote: Ensure law enforcement officers have the training, resources, and support necessary to protect our communities.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Safe Communities & Secure America Act page

candidates.name: Shelly Arnoldi

priorities.text: Defending parental rights and putting parents at the center of education decisions.
priorities.quote: put parents back at the center of education and defend parental rights

priorities.text: Cutting waste, taxes and red tape for families and small businesses.
priorities.quote: cut waste, taxes, and red tape so families and small businesses can breathe

priorities.text: Term limits and transparent budgets; she says she has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge.
priorities.quote: push term limits and transparent budgets (I've already signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge and I'll keep it)

statements.quote: enforce immigration laws and stop taxpayer-funded benefits for illegal immigrants
statements.context: In her answer on day-one priorities, Patch candidate questionnaire (Sept. 2026)

candidates.researchNotes: Found her campaign website (priorities page) and a Patch candidate questionnaire; her statements are general and only one touches a guide issue (immigration enforcement), without a stated position on the guide's statement. No statements found on abortion, guns, health care, taxes on high earners or other guide issues.

candidates.name: Tim Sharman

priorities.text: Affordability: housing, childcare, healthcare, education, groceries and transportation.
priorities.quote: I will focus on the things people worry about when they wake up in the morning: whether they can afford a home, childcare, healthcare, education, groceries and transportation

priorities.text: Introducing an "American Opportunity Fund Act" on day one.
priorities.quote: On Day 1, I will introduce it.

priorities.text: Never voting to shut down the federal government and supporting reforms to end shutdowns.
priorities.quote: I will never vote to shut down the federal government.

priorities.text: Health care reform, including a proposed "United States Healthcare Service."

positions.summary: Says women should have the right to choose, with legal limits: supports state-set gestational limits of about 16 weeks, with exceptions for serious medical circumstances.
positions.quote: I believe women should have the right to choose whether to terminate a pregnancy, but that right should have reasonable limits. I support allowing states to establish gestational restrictions, with approximately 16 weeks being a reasonable limit

positions.summary: Supports universal health coverage and proposes a public U.S. Health Service and automatic enrollment to be explored, while saying it should be pursued without new taxes.
positions.quote: I also believe we should try to achieve universal healthcare without imposing new taxes.

positions.summary: Says his proposed opportunity fund would be voluntary and that wealth creation should not be met with added taxes.
positions.quote: Financial success and wealth creation should be celebrated, not punished with added taxes.

statements.quote: Restricting the supply of offensive weapons, particularly large ordnance, is one option. However, I would advocate a more fundamental approach: embedding U.S. military personnel within IDF operational command structures, with authority to veto proposed military operations in Gaza.
statements.context: On his campaign website, "The Toughest Issues of Our Time"

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his campaign website (issue sections and 'The Toughest Issues of Our Time') and a Patch candidate questionnaire. No statements found on guns, immigration, climate, rent regulation or school choice.

researchNotes: Sabio's and Beyer's campaign-website quotes are drawn from Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and staff-curated profile respectively, which cite and quote their own campaign materials. Arnoldi and Sharman have no public campaign materials found beyond their ballot listing and FEC filings. Biography gaps: no biographical details were found for Sharman, and Sabio's campaign website could not be loaded, so his biography relies on Ballotpedia and news reports.
